# Docker sessions: DockerProvisioner and GM_SESSION_RUNTIME

## What to build

Once an open-source install has two or more accounts, every new session runs in its own Docker container, so users cannot read each other's files from a terminal. Add `DockerProvisioner implements SessionProvisioner` (`src/server/sessions/docker-provisioner.ts`), reusing the KAN-88 Docker code (`docker.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `sandbox-run.ts`, `sandbox-image.ts`): `acquire` starts container `gm-s-<sessionId>` from the session owner's sandbox image, with the user's own volume `gm-user-<safe id>` at `/workspaces`, the tools mount, the gm-clis mount and a new agent-runtime mount, env `GM_AGENT_TOKEN=<random>`, command `graph-manager agent --port 7700 --workspaces /workspaces`; it waits for `/agent/v1/healthz` and returns a `RemoteWorkspaceHost`. `release` removes the container, never the volume. `acquireRun`/`releaseRun` do the same for run containers `gm-r-<runId>` with the owner's `sandboxLimits`. A `RuntimeProvisioner` picks local or docker per `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME` (`auto` default, `local`, `docker`) and the account count, each time a session is opened (`auto` = local with one account, docker with two or more). In docker mode, if Docker is not reachable, opening a session answers 503 with the exact message below. Nothing under `packages/graph-execution/src` may change.

What dependencies already delivered (read these files first):
- Workspace host (`src/server/host/types.ts`, `host/local.ts`, `host/contract.ts`): `WorkspaceHost`, `HostError(status, message)` (the app error handler answers any `HostError` status with `{ error }`, including 503), `LocalWorkspaceHost`, `AppContext.hostFor(workspaceId, user)`.
- Workspace agent (`src/server/agent/server.ts` `startAgent({ port, host?, workspacesDir, token, ... })`, `src/server/agent/cli.ts` `runAgentCli`, `src/server/cli.ts` with the `agent` subcommand, `src/server/host/remote.ts` `RemoteWorkspaceHost(url, token)` with `viewTarget(workspaceId, runId)`).
- Sessions core (`src/server/sessions/provisioner.ts`: `SessionProvisioner { acquire({ user, sessionId }); release({ user, sessionId }); acquireRun({ user, sessionId, runId }); releaseRun({ user, runId }) }`, `LocalProvisioner`; `src/server/sessions/sessions.ts` `SessionManager`; `src/server/routes/sessions.ts` `POST /api/sessions`; session records in `Data.sessions` `{ id, repo: RepoRef, workspaceId, branch, state, startedAt, error? }`; `AppContext.provisioner`, `AppContext.sessions`; `buildApp` option `provisioner?: SessionProvisioner`).
- Accounts (`src/server/accounts.ts`: `countUsers(db)`, `getUser`, …) and db-store (`AppContext.db: Db`, `ctx.store.forUser(user)`, test helpers `memoryDb()`, `testStore()`, `appWithLogin`).
- db-store changed `Sandboxes` to be constructed with `{ store: UserStore, instanceId }` and left a TODO for per-user sandboxes: this task resolves it for sessions and run containers by reading the session OWNER's `UserStore` for the image (`workspaceSettings`, `sandboxRecipe`) and `sandboxLimits`.
- If the gateway task added `ctx.userLifecycle` (`src/server/userlifecycle.ts`, `onDisable(fn)` / `onDelete(fn)` with `fn(userId) => Promise<void>`), register `onDisable` (and `onDelete`) to remove that user's `gm-s-*` and `gm-r-*` containers (labels below); if that file does not exist yet, skip this wiring.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/provisioner.ts`, `sessions/sessions.ts`, `routes/sessions.ts` — where `acquire`/`release` are called and how errors propagate (a thrown `HostError` must reach the client with its status).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.ts` (lines 29–41 `ContainerInfo` incl. `Config.Env` and `NetworkSettings.Ports`, 199–330 `ping`, `inspectContainer`, `createContainer`, `putArchive`, `startContainer`, `removeContainer`, `waitContainer`, `containerLogs`, `listContainers(label)`, `createVolume(name, labels)`, `inspectVolume`, `removeVolume`, `buildImage`, `inspectImage`) — the client to use.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts` (lines 39–54 constants, 158–200 class fields/constructor, 221–233 `status()`, 398–404 `imageFor`, 481–495 `toolsDir`/`toolsMount`/`clisMount`, 505–697 `start()`: image checks, `imagePath`, owner, `docker.inspectContainer(name)` of an old container, env, mounts, `containerBody`, `putArchive`, the ready wait with logs on failure; 777–805 `pageOf`: published port vs container IP on `gm-sandbox`; 837–899 `doInit`) — the container lifecycle to mirror.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts` (lines 23–50 `SANDBOX_HOME`, `sandboxPath`, `LOGIN_FILES`; 150–205 `sandboxEnv`; 296–343 `containerBody`: `Init`, `SecurityOpt: ["no-new-privileges"]`, limits, `NetworkMode: "gm-sandbox"`, `PublishPort`) — container body pattern.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-image.ts` (lines 15–28 labels and targets, 38–58 `cliDockerfile`/`dockerContext`, 61–113 `ensureCliImage`/`ensureClisVolume`: build an image, fill a named volume by mounting it in a passive `Cmd: ["true"]` container) — the pattern for the agent runtime image and volume.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-tools.ts` (lines 10–23, 125–177 `copyEngine`, `fillTools`) — copying the engine.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tar.ts` (`TarEntry`, `tarArchive(entries, owner)`) — build contexts and the home folder entry.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` (lines 8–24 `Config`, 95–129 `envSchema`/`loadConfig`) — add `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME` (add, do not rewrite: sibling tasks add their own variables).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/docker.test.ts` (lines 1–45) and `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs` (lines 1–10, 101–140, 279–360: passive vs `exec` mode, `requests`, `containers`, `volumes`, `builds`) — the fake Docker for tests.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.docker.test.ts` (lines 1–45) — the real-Docker test skip pattern.
- `packages/graph-execution/package.json` `dependencies` — the agent runtime installs exactly these (they are graph-manager's server dependencies too, see bundle-imports.test.ts).

## Patterns to follow

**Exact constants:**
```ts
export const DOCKER_SESSIONS_DOWN =
  "Sessions need Docker when this graph-manager has more than one account. Start Docker, or set GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=local if everyone here trusts each other.";
export const AGENT_PORT = 7700;
export const SESSION_UID = 1000; // containers run as 1000:1000, never root, never privileged, no Docker socket
export const SESSION_LABEL = "gm.session"; export const RUN_CONTAINER_LABEL = "gm.run-container"; export const USER_LABEL = "gm.user";
```

**Docker-safe user id (volume `gm-user-<id>`):**
```ts
export function dockerSafeId(id: string): string {
  const slug = id.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9_.-]/g, "-").replace(/^[^a-z0-9]+/, "").slice(0, 40) || "u";
  const hash = createHash("sha256").update(id).digest("hex").slice(0, 8);
  return `${slug}-${hash}`;
}
// volume: `gm-user-${dockerSafeId(user.id)}`  (e.g. "admin" → "gm-user-admin-8c6976e5")
```

**Error handling:** Docker ping fails in docker mode → `throw new HostError(503, DOCKER_SESSIONS_DOWN)`. `sandboxes.status()` building → `HostError(409, "the sandbox image is building; try again when it is ready")`; other unavailable → `HostError(503, status.reason)`. Container exits before healthy / not healthy within 60 s → read `containerLogs(id, 20)`, remove the container, `HostError(502, `the session container exited with code ${code}`)` / `HostError(502, "the session container did not start within 60 s")` (log tail appended after a newline).

**Container body (session):**
```ts
{
  Image: image,
  Hostname: `gm-s-${sessionId}`.slice(0, 63),
  User: `${SESSION_UID}:${SESSION_UID}`,
  Env: [`GM_AGENT_TOKEN=${token}`, `HOME=${SANDBOX_HOME}`, `PATH=/opt/gm-agent/bin:${sandboxPath(imagePath)}`,
        "GM_GRAPH_EXECUTION_BIN=/opt/gm-tools/graph-execution/dist/cli.js", ...TZ/LANG from process.env when set],
  Cmd: ["graph-manager", "agent", "--port", "7700", "--workspaces", "/workspaces"],
  WorkingDir: "/workspaces",
  Labels: { "gm.session": sessionId, "gm.user": user.id },
  ExposedPorts: { "7700/tcp": {} },                          // only when graph-manager is NOT in Docker (!sandboxes.self)
  HostConfig: { Init: true, Privileged: false, SecurityOpt: ["no-new-privileges"], NetworkMode: "gm-sandbox",
    Mounts: [ { Type: "volume", Source: userVolume, Target: "/workspaces" }, toolsMount, clisMount,
              { Type: "volume", Source: agentVolume, Target: "/opt/gm-agent", ReadOnly: true } ],
    PortBindings: { "7700/tcp": [{ HostIp: "127.0.0.1", HostPort: "" }] } }  // only when !sandboxes.self
}
```
Never mount the Docker socket, the host's home, or the server's login files: a user's agent logins reach the container only through `host.loginFiles("put", …)` (agent-logins task). Before `startContainer`, `putArchive(id, "/", tarArchive([{ path: "home/sandbox/", dir: true, mode: 0o700 }], { uid: SESSION_UID, gid: SESSION_UID }))` so HOME exists and is writable.
Agent URL after start (mirror `pageOf`, sandbox.ts 795–804): not in Docker → `http://127.0.0.1:<NetworkSettings.Ports["7700/tcp"][0].HostPort>`; in Docker → `http://<Networks["gm-sandbox"].IPAddress>:7700`.

**Agent runtime (image + volume, mirroring ensureCliImage/ensureClisVolume):** `src/server/sessions/agent-image.ts`:
- `agentContext(serverDir, engineDir)`: a tar (`tarArchive`, owner 0:0) of `Dockerfile`, `package.json` = `{ "name": "gm-agent", "private": true, "type": "module", "dependencies": <packages/graph-execution/package.json dependencies, read from engineDir> }`, `server/**` = graph-manager's built `dist/server` folder (the folder of the running `cli.js`), and `engine/**` = the engine as `copyEngine` lays it out (dist + package.json).
- Dockerfile:
  ```
  FROM node:24.22.1-bookworm
  COPY package.json /opt/gm-agent/package.json
  RUN cd /opt/gm-agent && npm install --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund
  COPY engine /opt/gm-agent/node_modules/graph-execution
  COPY server /opt/gm-agent/server
  RUN mkdir -p /opt/gm-agent/bin && printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec node /opt/gm-agent/server/cli.js "$@"\n' > /opt/gm-agent/bin/graph-manager \
   && chmod 755 /opt/gm-agent/bin/graph-manager && mkdir -p /workspaces && chown 1000:1000 /workspaces
  ```
  (the full bookworm image has python3/make/g++ for node-pty).
- Tag `gm-agent:<first 12 hex of sha256(context)>`, labels `gm.sandbox-image` + instance like `ensureCliImage`; build only when missing. Volume `gm-agent-<image id hex 12>` filled from the image's `/opt/gm-agent` by a passive `Cmd: ["true"]` container (copy of `ensureClisVolume` with target `/opt/gm-agent`).
- A user volume that does not exist yet is created with labels `{ "gm.user": user.id }` and filled the same way from the agent image at target `/workspaces` (Docker copies the empty, 1000-owned `/workspaces` into the new volume, so the session user can write it).
- When `dist/server/cli.js` is missing (running from source) → `HostError(503, "graph-manager is not built: run npm run build -w graph-manager")`. Inject the whole runtime step in tests (option `agentRuntime`).

**Test pattern:**
```ts
// docker.test.ts lines 33–41: a fake Docker per test
fake = await startFakeDocker();           // passive mode: containers "run" until removed; Cmd ["true"] exits 0
docker = new DockerClient(fake.socketPath);
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `Config.sessionRuntime: "auto" | "local" | "docker"` from `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME` (default `auto`); any other value → `ConfigError('GM_SESSION_RUNTIME must be "auto", "local" or "docker"')`. Add only this variable; keep siblings' additions. Update `testConfig` in test-helpers.ts only if the type requires it (make the field optional with default `auto` if simpler).
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- config`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: resolve the per-user TODO for this path: add `imageForData(data: Data, wsId: string): { source: ImageSource; image: string }` (the logic of `imageFor`, lines 398–404, on a given user's data; `imageFor` calls it with its own store's data) and use the user's `sandboxRecipe` for the global image when the user has their own recipe (read how `defaultImage()`/`recipe()` read the store; if the user's recipe image does not exist yet, answer `HostError(409, "the sandbox image is building; try again when it is ready")` after `queueWorkspaceBuild`-style queuing, or fall back to `defaultImage()` when the user has no recipe). Expose `self` (already public) and keep everything else unchanged.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/agent-image.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `agentDockerfile()`, `agentContext(serverDir, engineDir)`, `ensureAgentImage(docker, ctx, instance)`, `ensureAgentVolume(docker, image, instance)`, `ensureUserVolume(docker, agentImageTag, user)` as described. Export `AgentRuntime = { imageTag: string; volume: string }`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/docker-provisioner.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  ```ts
  export interface DockerProvisionerOptions {
    config: Config; store: Store; sandboxes: Sandboxes; docker?: DockerClient;
    agentRuntime?: () => Promise<AgentRuntime>;                         // tests stub it
    waitReady?: (url: string, containerId: string) => Promise<void>;   // default: poll GET <url>/agent/v1/healthz every 250 ms, 60 s, checking the container still runs
    hostOf?: (url: string, token: string) => WorkspaceHost;            // default: new RemoteWorkspaceHost(url, token)
  }
  export class DockerProvisioner implements SessionProvisioner { … }
  ```
  - `acquire({ user, sessionId })`: `docker.ping()` (fail → 503 `DOCKER_SESSIONS_DOWN`); `sandboxes.status()` checks; `const us = await store.forUser(user)`; the session record `us.get().sessions[sessionId]` gives the workspace id for the image (`sandboxes.imageForData(us.get(), workspaceId)`; no record → the user's global image); runtime; user volume; remove a stopped leftover `gm-s-<sessionId>` (a running one → reuse it: token from `Config.Env` `GM_AGENT_TOKEN=`); token = `randomBytes(32).toString("hex")`; create, home archive, start, URL, wait ready (on failure remove the container and throw); return `hostOf(url, token)`.
  - `release({ sessionId })`: `removeContainer("gm-s-<id>", { force: true })`, ignoring 404 (`DockerError` status 404). Never removes the volume.
  - `acquireRun({ user, sessionId, runId })`: like `acquire` with name `gm-r-<runId>`, labels `{ "gm.run-container": runId, "gm.session": sessionId, "gm.user": user.id }`, a fresh volume `gm-r-<runId>` (filled from the agent image at `/workspaces`, label `gm.run-container`) instead of the user volume, and `NanoCpus`/`Memory`/`PidsLimit` from `us.get().sandboxLimits` exactly as `containerBody` computes them (sandbox-run.ts 325–327). Idempotent: a running `gm-r-<runId>` is reused (token from its `Config.Env`), so a restarted control plane can re-attach to a live run container.
  - `releaseRun({ runId })`: remove container `gm-r-<runId>` and volume `gm-r-<runId>` (ignore 404).
  - `releaseUser(userId)`: remove every container with label `gm.user=<userId>` (via `listContainers("gm.user")` filtered by label value). Register it with `ctx.userLifecycle.onDisable`/`onDelete` when that exists.
- **IMPORTS**: `../docker.js`, `../sandbox.js`, `../sandbox-run.js` (`SANDBOX_HOME`, `sandboxPath`), `../tar.js`, `../host/remote.js`, `../host/types.js`, `./provisioner.js`, `./agent-image.js`, `node:crypto`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/runtime.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  ```ts
  export function chooseRuntime(setting: "auto" | "local" | "docker", accounts: number): "local" | "docker" {
    return setting === "auto" ? (accounts >= 2 ? "docker" : "local") : setting;
  }
  export class RuntimeProvisioner implements SessionProvisioner {
    constructor(p: { setting: Config["sessionRuntime"]; countUsers: () => Promise<number>; local: SessionProvisioner; docker: SessionProvisioner }) {}
  }
  ```
  `acquire` decides per call (`chooseRuntime(setting, await countUsers())`), remembers `sessionId → provisioner` in a Map, and delegates; `release` uses the remembered one (unknown id → call docker.release, which ignores a missing container, then local.release). So a session started local keeps running local after a second account appears. `acquireRun` delegates to the provisioner of its session (remember `runId → provisioner`); `releaseRun` likewise (unknown → docker).
- **UPDATE `app.ts`**: when `opts.provisioner` is not given, `ctx.provisioner = new RuntimeProvisioner({ setting: config.sessionRuntime ?? "auto", countUsers: () => countUsers(ctx.db), local: <the LocalProvisioner the sessions task builds there>, docker: new DockerProvisioner({ config, store: ctx.store, sandboxes: ctx.sandboxes, docker: ctx.sandboxes.docker }) })`. Keep `opts.provisioner` overriding everything (tests and the commercial repo).

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/docker-provisioner.test.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT** (fake Docker in passive mode; `agentRuntime` stubbed to `{ imageTag: "gm-agent:test", volume: "gm-agent-test" }`; `waitReady` stubbed to resolve; `hostOf` returning a recording stub; `sandboxes.status` stubbed `available: true` with `vi.spyOn`, `toolsMount`/`clisMount` stubbed to known mounts):
  1. `acquire` creates exactly one container named `gm-s-<sessionId>` with `Cmd` `["graph-manager","agent","--port","7700","--workspaces","/workspaces"]`, an `Env` entry `GM_AGENT_TOKEN=<64 hex>`, `User` `1000:1000`, `HostConfig.Privileged` false, no mount whose Source contains `docker.sock`, a volume mount `gm-user-<dockerSafeId(id)>` at `/workspaces`, labels `gm.session`/`gm.user`; the token passed to `hostOf` equals the env token.
  2. `release` removes the container and the user volume still exists (`fake.volumes`).
  3. A second user's session uses a different volume; `dockerSafeId("Ann@Example.com")` matches `/^ann-example.com-[0-9a-f]{8}$/` and two ids differing only in case get different names.
  4. `acquireRun` creates `gm-r-<runId>` with the user's `sandboxLimits` (`NanoCpus`, `Memory`, `PidsLimit`) and its own `gm-r-<runId>` volume; `releaseRun` removes both; calling `acquireRun` again while it runs reuses it (no second create request).
  5. Docker down (a `DockerClient` on a socket path that does not exist) → `acquire` rejects with `HostError` status 503 and message `DOCKER_SESSIONS_DOWN` exactly.
  6. `chooseRuntime("auto", 1)` → `local`, `("auto", 2)` → `docker`, `("local", 5)` → `local`, `("docker", 1)` → `docker`; `RuntimeProvisioner` releases a session through the provisioner that acquired it after the account count changes.
  7. Route level (`appWithLogin` with `{ sessionRuntime: "docker", dockerSocket: "<missing socket>" }`, default provisioner): `POST /api/sessions` (body as the sessions route expects, e.g. `{ repo: { forge: "github", owner: "octo", name: "hello" }, branch: { new: "gm/x" } }`) answers 503 with `{"error":"Sessions need Docker when this graph-manager has more than one account. Start Docker, or set GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=local if everyone here trusts each other."}`; with the default `auto` and one account it does not touch Docker (local session, as before).
  8. `config.test.ts`: `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=docker` parses; `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=k8s` → the exact ConfigError.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/docker-provisioner.docker.test.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: real Docker end to end, skipped (with a `console.warn` reason) unless Linux, `/var/run/docker.sock` answers `ping`, `node:24.22.1-bookworm` is present locally (never pull), and `dist/server/cli.js` exists — copy the skip block of `sandbox.docker.test.ts` lines 20–40. `acquire` for a test user, then through the returned host: `activity()` answers, `spawnPty` of `["sh","-c","id -u; ls -ld /workspaces"]` prints `1000`, `release` removes the container and keeps the volume; clean up the volume and the agent image at the end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME` accepts `auto` (default), `local`, `docker`; anything else stops startup with `GM_SESSION_RUNTIME must be "auto", "local" or "docker"`.
- [ ] With `auto` and one account sessions are local as today; with two or more accounts a new session runs in container `gm-s-<sessionId>` with the user's own volume `gm-user-<dockerSafeId(userId)>` at `/workspaces`; live local sessions keep running when the second account appears.
- [ ] Session containers run as 1000:1000, are not privileged, have `no-new-privileges`, never get the Docker socket, and reach the control plane only through the agent port 7700; the agent token is random per container.
- [ ] `release` removes the container and keeps the volume; `acquireRun`/`releaseRun` manage `gm-r-<runId>` with the owner's sandbox limits.
- [ ] In docker mode without Docker, `POST /api/sessions` answers 503 `{"error":"Sessions need Docker when this graph-manager has more than one account. Start Docker, or set GM_SESSION_RUNTIME=local if everyone here trusts each other."}`.
- [ ] A disabled or deleted user's containers are removed (when `ctx.userLifecycle` exists).
- [ ] Nothing under `packages/graph-execution/src` changes; no new npm dependency.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm test -w graph-manager -- docker-provisioner config`

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- docker-provisioner config sessions sandbox docker
git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution/src   # must be empty
```
